stem.en: A classmate says, "When people earn more, the demand for every good always rises." Which reply fits the chapter best?

text.en: Usually, but not always: people may buy less of a plain, cheaper good and switch to a better one.
Yes: with more money, people buy more of every good.
No: income does not change demand at all; only the price does.
No: when people earn more, the demand for every good falls.

explanation.en: A rise in income usually raises demand, because people can afford more at the same prices. But not for every good: a family that earns more may buy less of a plain, cheaper good and buy a better one instead. Income does change demand, so price is not the only thing that matters.

hints.en: Think of a cheap good that a family might buy less of once it earns more.
